test/control_plane/gates.test.ts::the relay targets the stage the gate is about to enter (target-only) > a relay enqueued ahead of the gate's stage is refused
test/control_plane/gates.test.ts::the predecessor check does not break recovery (target-only) > a re-enqueue after the stage advanced still returns the message in force
target_only_tests.note: Target-only tests translate no source case and are NOT counted as ported coverage. The first is the seam-liveness test docs/test-translation-conventions.md rule 5 requires: two ported cases replace gatesSeams.appendEvent to drive a commit race deterministically, and without this a refactor that made closeGate call the imported appendEvent directly would leave both of them green, because their assertions are about refusals and would still hold for the wrong reason. Confirmed by mutation: bypassing the seam turns it and both ported cases red. The second buys back a coupling the translation gave up -- the source parametrizes over GATE_OUTCOMES itself, while conventions rule 2 requires the target ids to be written out, so an outcome added to the taxonomy and not reflected in the id list is a failure here rather than a case that silently stopped existing. The third pins a DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE from interlock (D-0026): a relay enqueued ahead of the gate's stage is refused here and accepted there. It is target-only because interlock has no case for it -- the behaviour being pinned is continuo's, not the source's. The fourth pins the other half of D-0026: the predecessor check runs only when a relay is about to be CREATED, never on the idempotent re-enqueue, because the crash window enqueueRelay is idempotent for is exactly the one that moves the stage. A first draft checked before the lookup and broke that recovery path; confirmed by mutation that this test catches it.

entries.target_id: test/control_plane/gates.test.ts::section 9.2 -- the projection > a closure identity on the spine without a closure is refused
entries.reason: The source's cp.commit() after the hand-written event INSERT has no counterpart: Python's driver opens an implicit transaction before DML, better-sqlite3 has none -- every statement outside a transaction() block autocommits (txn.ts, D-0012), so the row is durable at the same point. One dropped line; every assertion kept.

inherited_limitations.topic: relayGaps never ages a gate type that has no policy_gate_stage_tolerance rows.
inherited_limitations.detail: plan_approval and risk_approval are seeded with no tolerance rows today, so the section 9.6 detector is silent about them in every stage and raises no incident class for the gap. This is a hole in the design's own query rather than a translation defect, and interlock pins it with a case of its own (test_an_unpoliced_gate_type_is_silently_never_aged), which is ported here. When the tolerance decision lands, that case is the one that fails.

inherited_limitations.topic: The detectors and the subject-gone sweep have no caller anywhere in src/.
inherited_limitations.detail: gatesNeedingAdvance, relayGaps, stalledRelays, gatesPastDeadline and sweepSubjectGone are the detection half only; there is no reconcile-pass driver, matching gates.py's own module docstring and interlock#74 acceptance criterion 6 (no scope creep -- no reconcile driver). relayGaps' rows also name no ball-holder owner: D-0032's remedy pass is absent upstream too.

inherited_limitations.topic: gates.py's bare ValueError sites become bare TypeError.
inherited_limitations.detail: gates.py raises an untyped ValueError in three places rather than one of its own refusal classes. The port raises TypeError, which is the convention already established in events.ts and migrator.ts for an untyped Python ValueError; JavaScript has no ValueError, and the typed refusal families are reserved for Python's own named exception classes. The distinction Python draws between TypeError and ValueError is therefore collapsed onto one class. No ported case asserts a message for these -- test_gates.py contains no match= anywhere -- so only the class is pinned.

inherited_limitations.topic: Edge is exported as a TypeScript interface, where gates.py exports a runtime dataclass.
inherited_limitations.detail: gates.py lists Edge in __all__ as a frozen @dataclass, so a Python consumer can construct one. The port's Edge is a compile-time type with no runtime existence; ADMISSIBLE is plain data typed by it. Nothing in either suite constructs an Edge, and the table is read, not built, by every caller.

inherited_limitations.topic: ADMISSIBLE's actorKinds and CLOSE_OUTCOME_STAGES' values are mutable Sets.
inherited_limitations.detail: The source uses frozenset. Object.freeze on the containing object does not freeze a Set, and freezing a Set does not block .add() -- so immutability here is type-level only, the same position recorded for policy.ts's THRESHOLD_KINDS. Not reachable from any ported case.

inherited_limitations.topic: Numeric reads use Number(), where Python applies no coercion at these sites.
inherited_limitations.detail: The port wraps twelve reads in Number() where gates.py uses the driver's value directly. For an INTEGER column the two agree; they differ only for a hand-damaged row whose stored value is not an integer, which no ported case can produce through the public API. Recorded here because the direction is the opposite of D-0021's usual one: the port coerces where the source does not, rather than declining to narrow where the source does.

inherited_limitations.topic: enqueueRelay does not check that the relayed stage follows the gate's current stage.
inherited_limitations.status: REPAIRED -- deliberate divergence from interlock (continuo D-0026)
inherited_limitations.detail: continuo refuses a relay whose target stage is not the one the gate is about to enter, taking the DIRECT predecessor from ADMISSIBLE's own advance edge rather than a hardcoded pair. interlock checks only that the target is a relayed stage, so a 'forwarded' relay can be enqueued and acked while the gate is still 'received', and the stale ack is then accepted against an answer it predates. The rule is the direct predecessor and not 'anything reachable', because reachable leaves the same hole open ('received' reaches 'forwarded'). Chosen on evidence: all twelve enqueue_relay call sites in interlock enqueue at the direct predecessor and there is no production caller, so nothing legitimate is blocked -- see D-0026, which also records that a later reconcile driver needing to enqueue ahead should relax this deliberately rather than treat it as inviolable. Pinned by a target-only test.

inherited_limitations.topic: The gate-closed event payload is built from a gate read outside the append transaction.
inherited_limitations.status: REPAIRED -- deliberate divergence from interlock (continuo D-0024)
inherited_limitations.detail: The closure now refuses if the gate advanced between the payload's read and the transaction's reload, so the audit event and the gate row it describes can no longer disagree. interlock commits both, and for an outcome admissible from both stages ('withdrawn', 'subject_gone') nothing notices. Note the sibling finding about enqueueRelay's missing predecessor check is NOT repaired here: its scope depends on what ADMISSIBLE's edges are taken to mean, which is an open question escalated rather than decided.
